Subject: OrbisHealth — Dedicated GPU fit assessment & runbook proposal

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation and helpful context. Below is a concise recap, the risks we heard, and proposed next steps so we can align internally and with your team.

Quick recap of your goals (my words):
- Move latency-sensitive inference for clinical-document summarization to a dedicated pool to remove noisy-neighbor p95 variability.
- Ensure tenant isolation and PHI boundary controls to satisfy your security team.
- Start with a pilotsized capacity that can scale to steady-state traffic over Q4 (expected growth ~3–4x).

Pain points you described:
- Peaky loads during chart ingestion windows leading to degraded p95/p99 latency and timeouts for downstream services.
- Current multitenant provider not giving sufficient isolation guarantees (audit/segmentation ask).
- Need to validate inference quality after quantization — you can’t drop accuracy on critical summarization prompts.

Technical constraints (from call):
- Typical request: ~512 tokens gen, avg output 150 tokens; peak concurrent requests estimated 60–90.
- PHI in inputs, so VPC/KMS controls + SOC2 evidence will be required.
- Procurement lead time: 6–8 weeks once SOW and pricing are agreed.

Proposed pilot and runbook (attached):
1) 2-week pilot on an isolated dedicated pool (1–2 GPU nodes depending on model), focused on latency and correctness checks.
2) Baseline SLOs for pilot: p50/p95/p99 latency targets and token-level cost estimate; shadow traffic test before cutover.
3) Security checklist & evidence handoff to your compliance team (we’ll complete the questionnaire you send).
4) Post-pilot: sizing exercise for committed capacity + optional burst plan.

Attachments: isolation_runbook_draft.pdf (first-pass runbook), sow_estimate_Orbis_2027.pdf (ballpark SOW and pricing).

Next steps (asks):
- Samir/Elena: confirm procurement contact (copied ok) + any additional stakeholders for security.
- If agreeable, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with Marcus and Grace (30–45m) to lock in kernel/quantization options and pilot acceptance criteria.
- We'll send a small set of test prompts and metric collection instructions before pilot start.

Available times: I’ve added a quick scheduler link (below) — if you prefer calendar invites, send preferred times.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,

Looping in technical notes from infra/serving side so Samir/Elena have visibility:

- Model/quantization: for a first pass we recommend int8 quant + residual float16 validation for the most sensitive prompts. That will likely keep token cost low while preserving ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summaries — but we need your eval set.
- Sizing: given 512-token sequences and peak 80 concurrent, ballpark for a medium transformer model (7–13B family) is 2 x A100-class GPUs to meet p95 in the ~200–350ms range; larger models or stricter p99 targets push toward 4+ GPUs. We will include both pilot and committed sizing options in the SOW.
- Isolation: we can offer a dedicated VLAN + tenant-level KV cache partitioning for PHI separation; KMS integration options include network-reachable HSM or customer-managed keys via our KMS connector.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: defined perf test (shadow replay), functional correctness on 200 prompt samples, and successful security/keys integration.

I’ll prepare a short tech appendix to attach to the runbook with suggested instance types and expected token throughput. Mateo — can you confirm whether Orbis can share a sanitized sample workload for our perf modeling?

– Marcus
